The prevention sciences graduate certificate combines skills with methods to understand how to reduce risk and promote health and healthy development.
There is an emphasis on examining social determinants of health with the aim of enhancing equity and decreasing disparities.
Additionally, this program provides intellectual development and training to a diverse community of students who can benefit from foundational and applied skills in health promotion and disease prevention but require flexible academic pathways (Strategic priority 2; Goal 1; Action 1).
This certificate can be completed to meet requirements in the Master's of Professional Studies program and the Master's of Public Administration program.
For the Master's of Professional Studies (30 credits total), students complete two certificates, and six additional credits of coursework.
The Prevention Science certificate can be included as one of the certificates toward completion of the degree.
For the Master's of Public Administration (36 credits total), students complete three certificates to complete the degree.

The Prevention Science certificate can be included as the third certificate the students complete towards their degree.
The certificate could also be taken as a stand-alone certificate for any interested students.
One of the key elements of prevention science is the partnership with key community stakeholders (both public and private) who can work together to develop and implement appropriate interventions that address today’s health-related challenges.
Using evidence-based practices, applied learning, and real-world scenarios, students will be able to explore a range of issues through the lens of promoting and protecting health (e.g., social justice, family trauma, substance abuse and/or other addictions).
Therefore, the interdisciplinary nature of the program aims to foster meaningful interactions amongst students who bring expertise from a variety of health backgrounds.

This program aligns with the URI strategic plan priorities and goals in several ways to include: 1) Strategic Priority 1 (Broaden Our Impact), Goal 1: Contribute to broad and deep impacts on the social, cultural, and economic ecosystems across Rhode Island, the nation, and beyond. 2) Strategic Priority 2 (Enhance Student Achievement), Goal 2: Increase graduate student enrollment and degree completion. 3) Strategic Priority 4 (Power the University of the Future), Goal 4: Expand research and new academic programs and services through an increased focus on revenue generation.
Offered completely online and asynchronously, this program targets working professionals across a myriad of health sectors who wish to advance within the workforce while still holding full-time jobs.
This will be attractive to students while meeting employers’ needs.
Additionally, the stackable design of this program highlights the intersection of specialties that employers look for while offering a flexible path for students.
Furthermore, the appeal of the in-state competitive tuition speaks to the accessibility of the program nationwide and beyond.

In this graduate-level course, students will be introduced to principles of Prevention Science and evidence-based approaches to improve the physical and mental well-being of individuals, families and communities.

HDF 513: Promotion of Healthy Adulthood and Aging (3 crs.) In this graduate-level course, students will learn: (a) the relationship between biopsychosocial factors and healthy aging (b) risk, resilience, and protective factors for physical and mental health in adulthood and later life.

With 38 states allowing medical cannabis and 23 states now having adult use markets, legal cannabis has become the fastest growing industry in the United States.
The legal cannabis workforce has tripled over the past five years, outpacing the height of the technology sector's job growth.
Cannabis retail sales are estimated to reach $33.6 billion in 2023 with an additional economic impact of $100.8 billion.
These estimates do not include the hemp nor cannabidiol (CBD) markets that have grown out of the federal legalization of cannabis containing less than 0.3% tetrahydrocannabinol (THC).
The rapid job growth represents a problem for employers and has created public health concerns due to the lack of qualified employees.
The graduate certificate in cannabis sciences aims to address these concerns by providing students with the current knowledge in cannabis pharmacology and skills in cannabis formulation, manufacturing, and analysis.
Graduates of the certificate will have the knowledge to evaluate, develop, and research cannabis products in terms of safety and function.

Specifically, graduates will be able to 1) relate concepts of pharmacology and pharmaceutics to the development and therapeutic use of cannabis products, 2) propose strategies for the development of safe, stable, and functional cannabis products that meet or exceed current regulatory frameworks, and 3) apply analytical and bioanalytical techniques to assess the quality of cannabis products and the presence of cannabis metabolites in biological matrices for pharmacological studies.
The certificate program aligns with the University's mission and Strategic Plan by aiming to be an innovator in cannabis science education.
Specifically, the certificate addressed Priority 1: Broaden our Impact by providing students with the skill and knowledge necessary to make meaningful impacts and drive innovation in the cannabis field by adding to the scientific understanding of cannabis, solving challenges with product safety and stability, and addressing the stigma of cannabis through rigorous scientific inquiries (Goal 1 Action 2).

This will be accomplished by exploring current evidence-based literature and immersing students in the real world techniques and processes of cannabis and related industries (Goal 2 Action 3).
Priority 2: Enhance Student Achievement will be meet by the program through the use of interactive teaching technologies, the design of active learning discussions and assignments, and the implementation of andragogical strategies (Goal 1 Action 1).
The certificate is being offered in the accelerated 7 week format through URIOnline making it accessible to working professionals, those seeking career advancement or change, and other nontraditional graduate students (Goal 1 Action 2).
The program is designed as a stand alone certificate, but also has the potential to form the technical component of a new professional science master's (PSM) degree (Goal 2 Action1).
The certificate will enable the RI workforce to meet the challenges of the expanding medical and recreational cannabis market in RI and provide an opportunity for alumni to gain expertise in the evolving field aligning with Priority 3: Foster an Inclusive Culture (Goal 1 Action 3).

Finally, for Priority 4: Power the University of the Future , the certificate will generate new revenue streams in three ways: as a new academic program, by creating four new online courses, and as the technical component of a new PSM degree to be proposed in the future (Goal 4 Action 1).
There is no overlap with other programs at URI.

The science of pharmaceutical development is essential to the process of bringing a therapeutic entity from compound discovery to treatment in humans.
Most importantly, it seeks to create dosage forms for the compound that are safely consumed by humans (and animals), are stable until ingested, release the active drug product efficiently, avoid detrimental biologic interactions, have a consistent response, and have a known and controllable safety profile.
Advances in the knowledge and uses of injectable, biotech products have added a significant complexity to the drug development process.
In comparison to small molecule drug products, biological molecules have four levels of structure considerations making the development process much more complex and challenging.
Currently, over 70% of the compounds in the bio/pharmaceutical insudstry's drug development pipeline are large biological molecules.
This is a rapidly evolving area mandating continued education for those holding entry level degrees.
Graduates will have the knowledge to design and articulate a whole team approach to the product life cycle of a candidate drug molecule from initial identification through commercial launch.

Specifically, students completing this on-line certificate program will be able to 1) Describe the design and challenges of the pharmaceutical product development process from initial concept to market as well as the roles and responsibilities of each operational group; 2) Implement cGMP regulations for pharmaceutical drug substance and drug product manufacture; and 3) Develop product development strategies to optimize the creation of novel pharmaceuticals in industrial settings.
The online Graduate Certificate in Pharmaceutical Development meets the Provost's academic priority for active e-learning via technology-enhanced pedagogy and online programs.
Further, italigns with key goals of URI's 2022-32 Strategic Plan.
One goal of this Plan is to enhance studentsuccess by equipping learners with skills that are in demand in an ever-changing world, which this proposed certificate program aims to achieve.
The Pharmaceutical Development certificate program also addresses this goal's strategy of facilitating the implementation of new learningpedagogies and the expansion of modes of course delivery and assessment by leveragingspace and time in new ways.

This program also addresses the Plan's goal for diversity and social justice, as the Certificate program curriculum will include strategies for reducing genetic disparities in drug design, and for optimizing the use of pharmaceutical development resources to programs that serve vulnerablepopulations.
Additionally, this certificate program will augment knowledge in health and the STEM sciences, and develop the workforce to enhance public safety, as described in the Plan's goal to expand research, scholarship, and creative work.
